messages.content:
You choose building blocks for a board game rules engine. Rank the candidate mechanics and reference
games by how directly the described game needs them: first what it cannot be built without, then a close reference
game, then generally useful helpers. Leave out candidates that do not fit the game at all.

Game idea: send your workers to claim action spots on the farm; once a spot is taken nobody else can use it

Candidates:
- mech:worker-placement: Worker placement. Take turns sending workers to action spaces; an occupied space is blocked for everyone else this round.
- game:highsail: Highsail (worker placement and majorities). Original worker-placement game: send airship crews to action spaces on a skyport, where a taken space is blocked, to gather timber, crystal, fuel and coins. Take charters from an office row and launch them for points, income every round or end-game bonuses; each launch and each surveyed outpost adds to the majorities on five sky islands, which score after the middle and last rounds.
- mech:card-drafting: Card drafting. Pick one card from a hand and pass the rest to your neighbor until all cards are taken.
- mech:track: Track movement. Pawns move forward along a looping track of squares by a rolled amount, each player entering at their own start square and going once around to home.
- game:race-home: Race Home (Pachisi-style race). Roll a die and race pawns once around a looping track into home; landing on a rival sends it back to base, start squares are safe, a six rolls again, and a round limit ends long games.
- mech:capture-by-landing: Capture by landing. Landing exactly on an opponent's pawn sends it back to start; safe squares protect pawns.
- mech:simultaneous-selection: Simultaneous action selection. Everyone secretly picks an action at the same time, then all are revealed and resolved together, as in rock-paper-scissors.
- mech:flanking: Flanking capture. Placing a piece flips every straight run of rival pieces it traps between itself and another of your own pieces; only placements that flip something are legal.
- game:wildmere: Wildmere (tile placement and regions). Original tile-laying game: take hex tiles from a market row, where skipping tiles costs funds, then turn each one and lay it next to a growing valley so terrain edges match. Matching edges pay funds and join woodland, meadow, wetland and heath into regions; a region scores as soon as it is enclosed, one point per tile to whoever laid the most of it, and rangers add weight to a claim.
- mech:face-down-claims: Face-down claims and doubt. Play cards face down while announcing what they are; the next player accepts or doubts, and the pile goes to whoever was wrong.
- mech:bidding: Escalating bids and challenges. Players make ever-higher claims about hidden information; the next player raises the bid or calls liar, and the loser of the challenge is penalized.
- mech:open-auction: Open auction. Players bid money openly for an item; the highest bidder pays and takes it. English auction, once-around, sealed bids.
- mech:tile-placement: Tile placement. Draw a tile and place it adjacent to existing tiles so edges match, building a shared map that scores features.
- mech:gravity-drop: Gravity drop placement. Pieces are dropped into a column and fall to the lowest empty cell, as in drop-in-column games. Players choose a column, not a cell.
- mech:push-your-luck: Push your luck. Keep rolling or drawing to build up points this turn, but one bad result busts and loses them all; stop any time to bank.
- game:i-doubt-it: I Doubt It. Players play cards face down claiming the rank whose turn it is; the next player accepts or doubts, and whoever was wrong picks up the pile. First to empty their hand wins.
- game:hex: Hex. Two players claim hexagons on a rhombus board, one linking top to bottom and the other left to right; someone always connects, and a swap rule balances the first move.
- mech:line-win: K-in-a-row win condition. Win by forming an unbroken straight line of k of your pieces horizontally, vertically or diagonally. Connect, align, row, five in a row.
- mech:connection: Connection win condition. Win by building an unbroken chain of your pieces that links two opposite sides of the board, checked with a breadth-first search over neighbors.
- game:line-up: Line Up (m,n,k-game). Players take turns claiming cells on a grid; first to make a straight line of k wins. Tic-tac-toe, gomoku, and with gravity a drop-in-column game.
